Review of /Users/mhidding/Code/diffexp_refactored/Docs/RewritePlan.md — Lens 1 (mathematical correctness of the sector-native design). Findings verified against DiffExp/, FeynmanTrick/, Docs/FeynmanTrickBananaStatus.md, Docs/FeynmanTrickBoxFamilyStatus.md, Tests/*_Matrices, and /tmp campaign logs.

1. BLOCKER — Section 3.2 (Indicial.m, Solve.m) + M3: no module handles higher-order poles, but banana L1 (an already-validated in-scope example) requires it. Indicial.m is specified as "residue extraction A_{-1}(eps) at a chart", i.e. simple poles only. Docs/FeynmanTrickBananaStatus.md states the banana level-1 system at xx1 = 0, 1 "is the first place where a nilpotent DOUBLE pole and 5-fold resonant residues appear"; the old code copes via `FuchsianizeLocal`/`TrimFuchsianLattice` (DiffExp/LocalSeries.m:15-16, 183-260) — which live in LocalSeries.m, OUTSIDE the four files the plan counts as collapsing into the 600-line solver. Amendment: add an explicit local rank-reduction step (Moser/shearing or the lattice-saturation gauge transform) to Indicial.m or Solve.m with its own line budget (~200-300), a loud error when saturation does not terminate, and a banana-L1-endpoint pin in M3 (currently M3 lists only "a true-resonance log-chain case (banana endpoint)" — that same chart is the double-pole chart, so the test exists but the machinery to pass it does not).

2. MAJOR — Section 2 (I1) + Indicial.m + R1: linear-in-eps residue does NOT imply eigenvalues of the form a + b·eps. Counterexample: [[0,1],[eps,0]] is linear in eps with eigenvalues ±sqrt(eps). I verified the repo matrices are linear in eps (Tests/Banana_Matrices/dmm1_2..4.m and Tests/Hypergeometric2F1_Matrices/dz_2.m are zero matrices; box L2 confirmed linear in the campaign doc), but linearity of eigenvalues is a separate, stronger property. Amendment: I1 and Indicial.m must require that the characteristic polynomial of A_{-1}(eps) factors exactly as Π_i(λ − a_i − b_i·eps) over the rationals/algebraics, with a loud error otherwise; R1's trigger condition must be restated as "eigenvalues not linear in eps", not "residue not linear in eps".

3. MAJOR — Section 2 (I2) + Solve.m + 3.4: I2's claim that denominators "vanish ONLY for true resonances (same b, integer-spaced a)" ignores pseudo-resonances: integer-spaced a with DIFFERENT b. At step n with a_i + n = a_j, b_i ≠ b_j, the Frobenius denominator is exactly (b_i − b_j)·eps — a pure eps-Laurent SHIFT, so the homogeneous coefficient c[·,n] and everything it feeds gains one 1/eps of Laurent depth per such collision (the eps-symbolic image of the old eps^0 resonance; it has merely moved from "special machinery" to "window loss"). This configuration is realized in the validated examples: banana segment-1 endpoint mixes x^0, x^(−1+eps), x^(2·eps) sectors (Docs/FeynmanTrickBananaStatus.md, "Level-0 Fix" section), giving collisions (a=−1,b∈{1,2}) → (a=0,b=0) at n=1. Amendment: Solve.m must either (a) solve integer-spaced-a families jointly even when b differs, choosing the eps-regular combination at each collision (analogue of log-chain construction, keeping coefficients finite at eps=0), or (b) explicitly budget one Laurent order per collision pair in EpsWindow and in the 3.4 formula. Option (a) should be the spec; (b) silently degrades the windows.

4. MAJOR — Section 3.2 (Transport.m) + 3.4: the weight-matching linear solve is specified as a plain "linear solve in the sector basis", but the weights are genuinely eps-Laurent and the fundamental matrix can be singular at eps = 0. Standard example forced by these systems: log x = (x^(2eps) − 1)/(2eps) + O(eps) — a perfectly regular incoming function has 1/eps weights in the {x^0, x^(2eps)} basis whenever the eps→0 limit of the residue has a Jordan block that nonzero eps resolves (same a, different b, colliding eigenvectors). Then det F(t_m, eps) ~ eps^k, the solve is a Laurent inversion, and the honest-min window arithmetic loses k complete orders per such chart even though the transported function is complete to the full window (poles cancel in the assembled sum). Amendment: Transport.m must specify the matching as an eps-graded Laurent linear solve with (i) an assert on ord_eps det F (loud when > 0 unless handled), (ii) either a basis recombination that is unimodular at eps = 0 (use (S_i − S_j)/((b_i−b_j)eps) columns) or an explicit window-shift entry in EpsWindow; 3.4 must gain a per-singular-chart matching term or a proof obligation that the shift is zero.

5. MAJOR — Section 3.2 (Transport.m crossing rule): "per-sector phase e^(±iπ b eps)" is wrong/incomplete on three counts. (i) The phase is e^(±iπ(a + b·eps)), and non-integer a occurs (the old code special-cases half-integer powers: DiffExp/AnalyticContinuation.m:74-77). (ii) Log-chains mix under continuation: with the plan's normalization, (eps·Log t)^p/p! → Σ_{j=0}^{p} ((±iπ·eps)^j/j!) · (eps·Log t)^{p−j}/(p−j)!, i.e. the confluent family transforms into itself by a unipotent lower-triangular matrix M_{p→p−j} = (±iπ·eps)^j/j!; a sector with p > 0 does not just acquire a phase — it populates all lower-p sectors of the same (a,b). (iii) The convention must be pinned: the old rules use full-rotation factors (Logx → Logx − 2πi·θm, x^b → e^(−2πi b)·x^b on the θm side, AnalyticContinuation.m:71-78), which is the principal-branch-on-the-far-side convention, not the |t| convention where ±iπ appears; the 9aeb300 interior-split real-log lesson is exactly this. Amendment: write the crossing rule as the explicit (phase × p-mixing-matrix) operator and state which far-side coordinate convention (|t| vs principal branch) the coefficients use.

6. MAJOR — Section 3.2 (Integrate.m) + EpsSeries.m: the endpoint case table is incomplete and the stated closed form is wrong for p > 0. (i) ∫ t^(a+n+b·eps)(eps·Log t)^p dt produces denominators (a+n+1+b·eps)^(j+1) for j = 0..p; at a+n+1 = 0 this is a pole of depth p+1 in eps, not the single 1/(b·eps) the plan describes. (ii) The b = 0 loud-error condition must be a+n+1 ≤ 0 (power divergence at the t = 0 endpoint for a+n+1 < 0, and log^(p+1) divergence for a+n+1 = 0 with any p), not only a+n+1 = 0. (iii) The dimreg convention t^(a+n+1+b·eps)|_{t=0} := 0 for ALL a when b ≠ 0 (analytic continuation in eps) is load-bearing — it is the drop rule's integral counterpart — and is nowhere stated for Integrate.m. (iv) EpsSeries.m "div (series inversion)" must explicitly support Laurent division (denominator with vanishing eps^0 part → window shift: kmin and CompleteMax both drop by the shift); plain series inversion cannot produce 1/(b·eps). Amendment: full case table {b=0/b≠0} × {a+n+1 <0/=0/>0} × {p=0/p>0} in the Integrate.m spec, and a Laurent-division contract with window-shift semantics in EpsSeries.m.

7. MAJOR — Section 3.4: the budget formula is underspecified and not validated against the campaign's own numbers. Empirical record (/tmp/ft_box_bubble_run2.log:29,32): box_bubble single-level lower bounds were "needs 9" at L2 and "needs 11" at L1 — and the campaign's actual fix was to ABANDON per-level cutting and carry full incoming depth, because the single-level estimate "underestimates deep towers" (Scripts/run_ft_stepwise.m:154-161). Defects in the formula as written: (i) "|min eps-power of IBP coeffs|" is wrong when the min power is positive (should be Max[0, −minPower]); (ii) prefactorShift's sign convention and cumulative-vs-per-level semantics are undefined (the old code threads CUMULATIVE prefactors, FeynmanTrick/DiffExpIntegration.m:1460); (iii) "enhancements = number of b≠0 pole sectors" should be the maximum pole DEPTH max_i(p_i + 1) over pole-hit sectors per endpoint — several p=0 sectors give depth 1 total (overcounted), one p=2 sector gives depth 3 (undercounted); (iv) no terms for the window losses of findings 3 and 4; (v) interior iδ-crossed poles contribute no enhancement only if the two half-segment boundary terms are combined exactly ((e^(iπ b eps) − 1)/(b·eps) is regular) — state this. Amendment: define each term with signs, and add an M5 gate: "formula output dominates the box_bubble empirical bounds {L2: 9, L1: 11} and the banana IntegrationPoleAllowance=4 record, with EpsWindow loud-error as backstop."

8. MAJOR — Section 3.2 (SectorSeries.m): the multiplication closure claim is false for a denominator vanishing strictly inside the chart away from the center. Partial fractions of 1/(t − t1)^m with 0 < |t1| < Radius yields a Taylor series with convergence radius |t1|: the product is still representable but the chart's Radius MUST shrink to |t1|, and any matching/evaluation point beyond |t1| silently diverges (the ODE-residual spot-check does not cover products). Amendment: SectorSeries multiply contract: poles at the center shift a; poles with |t1| ≥ Radius fold into the regular part; poles with 0 < |t1| < Radius either shrink Radius (recorded) or are a loud error, with the Transport.m segmentation (matrix denominators + ExtraSingularFactors, cf. CollectLevelIBPSingularFactors) required to guarantee the error branch is unreachable. Also amend the 3.1 invariant "exactly one sector with a=0,b=0,p=0 at a regular chart": products with IBP coefficients violate it (a ≠ 0 at ODE-regular points); scope it to ODE solutions only.

9. MAJOR — Section 3.2 (Solve.m): the inhomogeneous particular at a true-resonant step is unspecified, and the old code is a broken oracle here. When the source sector tag satisfies a_s + n = a_i, b_s = b_i (denominator identically zero in eps), the particular requires a log-bump (p → p+1) in the ansatz; the box campaign hit exactly this (L1 endpoint sources "gain one Logx power per epsilon order", Docs/FeynmanTrickBoxFamilyStatus.md NormalizeLogPower section), and the box status doc lists "the general singular solver returns an empty particular ... for resonant-with-source inputs — currently bypassed, never properly fixed". Amendment: Solve.m spec must state the resonant-source log-augmentation rule explicitly and M3 must add a closed-form pin for it (∫x^(−1)·log^k x type), since no old-code parity oracle exists for this path.

10. MINOR — Section 3.1: Sector "Coeffs" is a 2D array (eps-order × t-power) and Value(x) is scalar, but the object must represent N-component master VECTORS (the matching solve and the ODE-residual invariant both need all components). Amendment: add the component index to Coeffs (c[k, n, comp]) or state that a LocalSolution holds one vector solution with per-sector vector coefficients.

11. MINOR — Section 3.1: "Prescription" holds a single Factor/Sign pair, but the old continuation logic handles multiple simultaneously vanishing prescription factors and detects sign conflicts (DiffExp/AnalyticContinuation.m:45-68, including the square-root-added-prescription distinction). Amendment: Prescription is a LIST of {factor, sign} with a conflict-detection loud error at chart construction.

12. MINOR — Section 3.2 (SectorSeries.m): "re-expand around a new center" has no truncation contract. The re-expansion of t^(a+b·eps)(eps Log t)^p around a regular center has an infinite t'-Taylor tail (and collapses exact b-structure into per-eps-order logs — fine for the pipeline since tags are always re-derived by fresh Frobenius at the next singular chart, but state this). Amendment: specify the target truncation order, a tail bound from the radius ratio (|Δcenter|/R)^N, and how this feeds the CurrEvalError-equivalent (ledger lesson is named in section 5 but not bound to this operation).

13. MINOR — Sections 3.2 (API.m), M5: the existing matrix-directory format is eps-SLICES truncated at a fixed order (FeynmanTrick/MatrixExport.m:42-77 writes d{var}_{0..epsOrder}.m via SeriesCoefficient, default epsOrder 4), which cannot certify the exactness/linearity that I1 and Indicial.m rely on — a rational-in-eps entry would be silently Taylor-truncated. Amendment: DiffExp2 LoadSystem for FT use must consume the exact symbolic export (ExportDiffExpMatrixFull's d{var}_full.m) or require an exactness attestation; slice directories are acceptable only for the classic per-order transport path.

14. MINOR — Section 3.1 + 3.4: with the (eps·Log t)^p/p! bundling, true-resonance log-chain solutions (b-equal, e.g. the banana L1 x=1/2 chart's genuine size-3 Jordan block, eigenvalues {0,0,0,0,1}) carry log^p t with eps-INDEPENDENT weights, forcing kmin = −p in those sectors' coefficient windows. This is representable (Laurent kmin) but nowhere stated, and the window/budget arithmetic must not treat negative kmin in homogeneous solutions as an error. Amendment: state in 3.1 that homogeneous true-resonant sectors have kmin = −p by construction, and exempt/account for this in EpsWindow propagation and the 3.4 formula.

# Review: RewritePlan.md — Lens 2 (legacy numerical wisdom)

1. **BLOCKER — §3.2 Indicial.m + §2 I1.** The contract "exact eigenvalues a_i + b_i eps (linear-in-eps residues; loud error otherwise)" fails the plan's own parity gates. Matrices are loaded as per-eps-order slices `d<var>_<ord>.m` (MatrixLoading.m:29,92): banana ships slices 0..4 (Tests/Banana_Matrices/dmm1_0.m..dmm1_4.m), so A_{-1}(eps) is **quartic** in eps; FT systems are **rational** in eps (IBP coefficients in d), truncated to slices by ExportDiffExpMatrix (MatrixExport.m:42-77, default epsOrder 4). With the contract as written, Indicial errors out on M2's "banana endpoints" and on every FT level system, so M2/M3/M4/M5 gates fail by design. Amend: residue entries are eps-rational/eps-polynomial; the loud error must trigger on **eigenvalues not affine in eps**, not on the residue matrix; I1's "exactly linear in eps for FT systems" claim is false and must be rewritten.

2. **BLOCKER — §3.2 API.m / §6 M5.** The plan never says which matrix format DiffExp2 consumes, but its central promise (exact b-spectrum, exact eps-Laurent recursion) is unachievable from the current FT export: the FT pipeline exports eps-**truncated** slices (MatrixExport.m:42-83). The exact-eps format already exists (`d<var>_full.m`, ExportGeneralMatrix, MatrixExport.m:91-114) but nothing consumes it. Amend §3.2 LoadSystem + M5 cutover: DiffExp2 loads the exact eps-rational matrix (full format; slices accepted only for legacy parity), and FT cutover switches MatrixExport to ExportGeneralMatrix. Otherwise "nothing ever needs fitting" degrades to "fitting replaced by truncation error".

3. **MAJOR — §3.1 "Prescription" field.** One `<|Factor, Sign|>` per chart is not what the old code needs or does. PrepareAnalyticContinuation (AnalyticContinuation.m:18-68) collects **all** DeltaPrescription factors vanishing at the chart center, derives a required Sign[Im x] per factor from (prescription sign) ÷ (sign of leading coefficient) and the **parity of the vanishing exponent k** (even k → "?", no constraint), then demands consistency across factors; inconsistency/indeterminacy sets AnalyticContinuationFailed → results valid only on one side (Transport.m:494-496). It also auto-adds +iδ for square-root factors found in the DEs (State.m:227-230, DEqnSquareRoots) distinct from user prescriptions, and crossing an unprescribed branch point errors loudly via the default-on SingularityCheck (Transport.m:470-492; CrosscheckFlags "SingularityCheck"->0, State.m:205). Amend the field to a derived record: list of (factor, prescribed sign, multiplicity k, leading-coeff sign) → consistency-checked single Im-sign; even-k = no constraint; conflict or missing prescription with b≠0/p>0 sectors = loud error. Ledger: "Per-chart iδ sign is derived from ALL vanishing prescription factors with multiplicity-parity and leading-coefficient-sign; must be consistency-checked, not stored as one factor."

4. **MAJOR — §3.2 Transport.m + §3.1 Radius.** Complex singularities are absent from the plan. FindMatrixSingularities solves all factors (complex roots included) and projects each complex root onto the real line as ghost points Re and Re±Im, suppressed if a real singularity already lies in the interval (LineSegmentation.m:81-99; Docs/Infrastructure.md:84-85); these cap chart radii and force segmentation, while `imaginarySingularities` distinguishes ghost centers (regular charts) from true ones (Transport.m:603,1014). Pentagon (5 prescription letters, FivePointNonPlanar_example.m:142-148) and the unequal-mass banana Källén-type denominators (Tests/Banana_Matrices) produce complex roots on generic lines. Amend: Radius = distance to nearest singularity **in the complex plane**; ghost-projection (or true complex-distance) logic in segmentation; ghost centers get regular charts, no Indicial. Ledger: "Chart radius must respect complex singularities; old code projects them to Re, Re±Im ghost points (LineSegmentation.m:81-99)."

5. **MAJOR — §3.4.** `enhancements(Lk) = number of b!=0 pole sectors at endpoints` is the wrong count twice over: ∫t^(-1+b eps)(eps Log t)^p dt produces 1/(b eps)^(p+1) — a log-chain endpoint pole enhances by **p+1**, while several plain (p=0) pole sectors each give only one inverse power that adds, not compounds. Replace with: enhancements(Lk) = max over endpoint sectors with a=-1, b≠0 of (p+1). The plan itself designates banana endpoints as true-resonance log-chain pins (M3), so p>0 at endpoints is in-scope before dbox.

6. **MAJOR — §5 seeds + §3.1.** No t-order (chart-order) honest-window analog of EpsWindow. The old code explicitly budgets x-order degradation from sequential block coupling: MaxCouplingOrder = longest coupled chain (MatrixLoading.m:383); matrix-truncation error is read at order ExpansionOrder − ISafetyExpansionSubtract − (MaxCouplingOrder−1) (LineSegmentation.m:109-113); evaluation error re-evaluates at order reduced by Ceiling[0.7·MaxCouplingOrder]+2 (State.m:222, Transport.m:913). The seed "error estimation (CurrEvalError) and ISafetyExpansionSubtract" omits the coupling-depth dependence. Losing it: weight-matching solves and error estimates trust top t-orders that are garbage after k inhomogeneous solves. Ledger: "Top (coupling-depth−1) t-orders of a chained particular solution are degraded; error estimation and matching must discount them (GetLargestTerm/ICurrEvalErrorSeriesDecrease formulas)."

7. **MAJOR — §3.2 Transport.m + API output.** Per-segment error estimation/accumulation is user-facing and missing from the new object/API: EstimateError="Fast" evaluates each segment at full and order-reduced truncation at **both** the matching point and eval point (avoiding x=0 because logs vanish there spuriously, Transport.m:915-922), per (integral, eps-order) and per symbolic indeterminate (ComputeErrorsPerIndeterminate, Transport.m:947-962), accumulates additively across segments, aborts when error > 1 (Transport.m:991-993), and returns "ErrorEstimates" that tests consume (test_multiple_polylogarithms.m:106-107, test_five_point_nonplanar.m:249). Amend §3.1/§3.2: an error-estimate field per LocalSolution and an ErrorEstimates output in API.m. Ledger: "Two-point full-vs-reduced-order error probe per segment, accumulated additively; abort at error>1."

8. **MAJOR — §3.4 + §5 seeds.** Predivision digit budgeting is missing: TransportTo dry-runs the whole segmentation to count segments (Transport.m:666-750), then sets DigitsNeeded = AccuracyGoal + Ceiling[Log10[#segments]] + ISafetyDigits (Transport.m:758-760). The static order budget covers eps orders only, not precision-vs-segment-count. Losing it: long lines (banana to t=10 through three thresholds) silently lose the accumulated-error digits. Ledger: "Per-segment accuracy target must be tightened by log10(segment count) (two-pass predivision counting)."

9. **MAJOR — §3.2 API.m.** "Mirrors old entry points where cheap" is too thin against what Reference/Examples and Tests actually call; M4/M6 parity requires: PrepareBoundaryConditions with closed-form eps expressions (auto eps-expansion, leading-asymptotics extraction along the line incl. x^(a+b·eps) scaling and Log→Logx rewriting, Transport.m:31-120) and per-integral `"?"` wildcards (ignore-this-integral's-bcs, Transport.m:63-65, consumed at IntegrateSystem Transport.m:288-292; used in Banana_example.m:32-33); TransportTo association chaining and **bidirectional** transport (to < FixAt); singular-endpoint mode returning the series instead of a value (Transport.m:605-613, 1053-1096; test_singular_endpoint.m); SaveExpansions + ToPiecewise (Banana_example.m:57,152, test_topiecewise.m); transport with symbolic indeterminate coefficients (auto-disables Pade, per-indeterminate error tracking, Transport.m:565-569); CurrentConfiguration/LoadConfiguration/UpdateConfiguration; both `eps` and `\[Epsilon]` accepted (MatrixLoading.m:118). List these explicitly as the M5/M6 API contract.

10. **MAJOR — §5 ledger seeds.** The plan must enumerate the kept config surface; nothing in §3 or §5 lists it. Live keys verified in code/examples: AccuracyGoal + "AccuracyGoalValidate" ("Before": adaptive expansion-order search loop with averaging window 3, ±10 steps, 3-digit surplus threshold, min order 10, Transport.m:776-841; "After": redo segment at +25, Transport.m:1191-1213), ChopPrecision (< WorkingPrecision invariant + LinearSolveChopPrecision auto-sync on every update, DiffExp.m:121-130), DeltaPrescriptions (±Iδ parsing + irreducibility validation, DiffExp.m:140-168), DivisionOrder, EpsilonOrder, EstimateError, ExpansionOrder, LineParameter, LogFile, MatrixDirectory, RadiusOfConvergence, RationalizationTolerance, SegmentationStrategy (decide Dynamic's fate explicitly; FT and defaults use Predivision), UseMobius, UsePade, Variables, Verbosity, WorkingPrecision, CrosscheckLevel/CrosscheckFlags, SaveExpansionsCompress(+Directory/+Order), "AbortOnAnalyticContinuationFail" (Transport.m:471), IgnoreIndicialCheck (Frobenius.m:42). Add a table: kept (DiffExp2 equivalent) / waived (reason). RationalizationTolerance and the FT 10^-40 absolute zero test (item 13) must fold into Tolerances.m or the "ONE module" claim is false on day one.

11. **MAJOR — §3.2 module map + R6.** Pade has no home in the module map despite being load-bearing: classic examples require UsePade->True (Banana_example.m:20,77; FivePointNonPlanar_example.m:151; resonant 2F1/banana tests), it is applied per-Logx-coefficient at evaluation (GetPade, Pade.m:32-53), and the error probe flows through the same path (Transport.m:905-925). Reason it exists: matching points sit at radius/DivisionOrder where plain partial sums converge slowly — accuracy per order, not luxury. R6's "within 2x of old on banana line" is benchmarked against a UsePade+UseMobius+RadiusOfConvergence->10 oracle. Either allocate Pade evaluation in Transport.m/SectorSeries (with its fallback made loud — GetPade currently warns and silently evaluates normally, Pade.m:44-46), or waive it in the ledger with a re-baselined benchmark. Separately add the missing seed: **RadiusOfConvergence chart rescaling** ("Without setting this option, the intermediate expansions blow up", Banana_example.m:75) — coefficient-magnitude control by rescaling the chart coordinate (Mobius.m:47,65). Ledger: "Chart-coordinate rescaling (RoC) keeps high-order coefficients O(1); banana requires RoC=10."

12. **MINOR — §5 seeds ("division-order heuristics").** Specify what DivisionOrder actually controls, since R3's conditioning mitigation depends on it: (a) matching/eval point at chart radius/k (Transport.m:679,1041,1046); (b) next-center placement solved so the previous eval point also sits at the 1/k fraction of the **new** chart (GetCPL/GetCPR, Mobius.m:98-142) — that geometric guarantee is the actual ill-conditioning defense; (c) segment count/digit budget (item 8). FT pins k=4 (DiffExpIntegration.m:272), classic default 3. Ledger: "Match point must sit at radius/k of BOTH adjacent charts (GetCPL/GetCPR geometry), not just the current one."

13. **MINOR — §3.4/§4 (FT honest-window subtleties beyond CompleteMax).** Port or explicitly kill: (a) LaurentTrim advances MinPower past "numerically zero" leading coefficients with an **absolute** 10^-40 test (DiffExpIntegration.m:1177-1189) — misclassification shifts the whole Laurent and the uniform per-level prefactor shift; must become a Tolerances.m-derived relative test; (b) ShiftRawBoundariesToFinite applies one uniform shift to all masters and zero-pads up to the level max (1258-1280) — partially covered by A1, state the replacement; (c) the "keep at least one output order" floor (658-661) masks an empty window — delete under A1; (d) silent `Quiet[Check[...,0]]` endpoint-evaluation fallbacks at DiffExpIntegration.m:1038-1059 and the Limit→substitution→0 chain at 1080-1093 are additional A1 sites beyond the one A1 names.

14. **MINOR — §3.2 Transport.m (crossing rule detail).** "per-sector phase e^(±iπ b eps) etc." underspecifies the old convention (AnalyticContinuation.m:70-79): sign **+1 applies no replacement at all** (relies on principal-branch Log/Power at negative argument — this pins which of ±iπ); sign −1 applies Logx → Logx − 2πi·θm (a **shift**, which mixes (eps Log t)^p log-chain members binomially, not a phase), half-integer powers via Sqrt with (θp − θm), and e^(−2πi b) only for denominator > 2. Spell out the p>0 mixing and the principal-branch pinning, plus the interior-split convention (9aeb300, already seeded).

15. **MINOR — §6 M4.** Parity checkpoints depend on the oracle's config (UseMobius/UsePade/DivisionOrder/RoC change segment structure and checkpoint locations). Pin the exact old-config per example in the M4 gate (e.g. banana = Banana_example.m's UnequalMassConfiguration).

16. **MINOR — §3.2 Integrate.m.** State whether Mobius charts are accepted by Integrate.m. The old FT integration hard-requires UseMobius->False ("Required for integration!", DiffExpIntegration.m:352). If DiffExp2 transport may use Mobius charts, Integrate.m must implement rational-map jacobians or reject loudly — silence here recreates exactly the class of seam the plan exists to kill.

17. **MINOR — §2 I2 / §5.** File references are wrong for the post-compaction contract: Recurrence.m/ResonantRecurrence.m/VOP.m live under `DiffExp/IntegrationStrategies/` (870+1527+304 lines) plus DiffExp/Wronskian.m (112) = 2813, reaching ~3.5k only with Frobenius.m (141) and IntegrationStrategies/{Default,Dispatch,Helpers}.m (453). Fix paths/counts so M0 ledger agents target the right files; also add LocalSeries.m (1026 lines) to the subsumed-by-Solve.m inventory or state its disposition.

18. **MINOR — §5 seeds ("precision raising of inputs").** Underspecified: inputs are raised to **2×**WorkingPrecision, not 1× (Transport.m:541-562; PrepareBoundaryConditions Transport.m:38-41; GetLineRescaled SetPrecision[...,2·WP], Mobius.m:48,66), and all evaluations run under `$MinPrecision = FEWorkingPrecision` blocks (Pade.m:34,70,80) with `$MaxExtraPrecision = 1000` (Mobius.m:39). Ledger: "Raise inputs to 2×WP and floor evaluation precision with $MinPrecision=WP; the 2× headroom is what survives chart-map composition."
